elements.reason: Main outcome results (AGREE II domain scores) presented for the 71 included CPGs.
No meta-analysis was conducted; review used descriptive AGREE II appraisal, so no summary estimate applies.

The abstract does not mention limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias or the AGREE II limitations of the guidelines.

elements.quote: Conclusion: Future CPGs for COVID-19 need to rely, for their development, on standard evidence-based methods and tools.
elements.reason: Abstract provides interpretation and implication of the findings.

The abstract does not provide registration name or number; PROSPERO registration appears only in Methods (text_3).

elements.quote: Although most COVID-19 cases recover without any major complications, some patients develop a progressive disease due to pneumonia and respiratory failure [6]. These patients are managed in Intensive Care Units (ICUs) and have high mortality rates, ranging between 25 and 40% [7].
elements.reason: The Introduction describes the current state of knowledge about COVID-19 critical illness and the existing CPG landscape, including uncertainties around rapid guideline quality.

elements.quote: Given the extraordinary burden that the pandemic has created on the emergency and critical care units worldwide, there is an urgent need for evidence-based guidance to facilitate optimal clinical and policy decisionmaking.
elements.reason: The importance and need for the review are explicitly explained, including the lack of assessment of CPGs for critically ill COVID-19 patients.

elements.quote: Four previous reviews have assessed the quality of COVID-19 CPGs [16-18]. ... However, an assessment of all the CPGs focused on the management of critically ill COVID-19 patients was lacking.
elements.reason: Similar prior reviews are identified and cited (Zhao et al., Dagens et al., Chiesa-Estomba et al., Luo et al.), and the gap justifying the current review is explained.
This is a review of clinical practice guidelines' methodological quality (AGREE II appraisal), not a review of intervention effects, so a mechanism of action description does not apply.
The review appraises guideline quality rather than evaluating complex interventions, so a logic model of intervention components and outcomes is not applicable.

elements.quote: Objective: We aimed to systematically identify and critically assess the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19 with the AGREE II instrument.
elements.reason: An explicit objective statement is provided at the start of the article (abstract section), clearly stating the aim of the review.

elements.quote: Objective: We aimed to systematically identify and critically assess the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19 with the AGREE II instrument.
elements.reason: This is a review appraising the quality of clinical practice guidelines with AGREE II, not a review of intervention effects requiring planned PICO comparisons.

elements.quote: For inclusion, CPGs had to provide specific recommendations for clinical management, diagnosis and/or treatment of critically ill patients with COVID-19. When more than one version was available, we included only the most updated version or edition of the eligible RGs.
elements.reason: The key eligibility characteristic (guidelines addressing critical care COVID-19 management) is specified, but eligible designs, settings, and framework components are not fully detailed.
No eligibility criteria regarding dissemination year, language, or publication status are reported in the Methods; language limitations are only mentioned post hoc in the Discussion.
This is a review of clinical practice guidelines, not primary studies with outcome data; the distinction between unmeasured and unreported outcomes does not apply.
No grouping of guidelines for syntheses is specified in the methods; extracted variables are listed (text_5) but no synthesis groups or comparisons are defined.
No rationale for eligibility restrictions (e.g., most updated version only, critical care focus) is provided in the retrieved methods text.

elements.reason: Search dates are reported for the databases and for the grey literature sources.

elements.quote: We extracted the following variables from each eligible CPG: ID (acronym or first author), country, economic classification, healthcare system, scope of the CPG, language, methods of development, date of publication, developer organization (if applicable), type of organization, target critical disease (specialty), CPG implementation tools, consideration of patients' views and preferences, the use of specific method to assess quality of the evidence (e.g. GRADE), and all options of therapeutic interventions for critically ill people with COVID-19 whether general supportive care or specific COVID-19 therapy, results of the AGREE II quality assessments
elements.reason: The methods section explicitly lists all variables sought during data extraction, including participant/guideline characteristics and funding-related organizational details.

No citation of a tool used to determine which data items to collect is provided; the variable list appears to be developed via internal focus group discussions rather than a cited tool.

elements.quote: Two reviewers conducted independent quality assessment of each eligible CPG with the AGREE II instrument
elements.reason: The tool (AGREE II) is explicitly named as the quality assessment instrument.

elements.quote: which consists of 23 items grouped in 6 domains, in addition to 2 final overall assessments. The six AGREE II domains are scope and purpose, stakeholder involvement, rigour of development, clarity of presentation, applicability, and editorial independence.
elements.reason: The domains and items of AGREE II are described in detail.

elements.quote: A final overall assessments... The scoring or rating of each CPG was performed using a 7-point Likert scale... The standardized domain score would be 0% if each appraiser scored 1 for all the items included in this domain
elements.reason: Overall assessments (OA1/OA2) are part of the tool and scoring rules (7-point Likert, standardized domain scores) are reported; discussion also notes ≥60% in D3 used for overall quality.
No adaptations to AGREE II are reported; the standard instrument was used.
No new risk-of-bias tool was developed; the established AGREE II instrument was used.

elements.quote: Two reviewers conducted independent quality assessment of each eligible CPG... Discrepancies in the scoring were resolved by focus group discussions facilitated by a CPG methodologist (YSA).
elements.reason: Number of reviewers (two), independence, and disagreement-resolution procedure are reported.
No evidence of processes to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information from guideline investigators; not applicable to this guideline-appraisal review.

The retrieved evidence describes a systematic review of clinical practice guidelines appraised with AGREE II; no effect measures (e.g., risk ratio, mean difference) are specified for any outcome in the synthesis or presentation of results.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect size or their rationale are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure are described in the retrieved evidence.
No justification for a choice of effect measure is provided; the retrieved evidence contains no discussion of effect measures at all.

elements.quote: One reviewer independently screened the retrieved titles and abstracts. A second reviewer screened the undecided and included for quality control. After the first screening, 2 reviewers screened the full text independently, and a third reviewer was invited to resolve disagreements.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the general eligibility criteria (text_3: CPGs providing recommendations for critically ill COVID-19 patients, most updated version) and the screening/selection process with reviewer roles and disagreement resolution (text_5). However, it does not describe processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each specific synthesis, such as tabulating guideline intervention characteristics and comparing them against planned synthesis groups (e.g., how guidelines were assigned to the therapeutic intervention categories shown in Tables 2A/2B).

elements.quote: We summarized the general characteristics of the CPGs with descriptive statistics. We present frequencies and proportions to summarize categorical variables used to describe the guidelines. We used mean and standard deviation (SD) to summarize the scores across all the guidelines per domain. ... We selected a cut-off for high quality CPGs of 60% or more for all the 6 AGREE II domains ... the cut-offs for low and moderate quality are < 40% and 40%-60%, respectively. For the overall quality of any CPG, whenever there was a discrepancy between OA1 and the mean score for all domains, we relied on the quality of the domain 3 score to upgrade or downgrade the overall score
elements.reason: The Data Analysis section describes several data preparation methods: summarization with descriptive statistics, conversion of AGREE II 7-point Likert item ratings into standardized percentage domain scores (text_6), categorization of guideline quality using explicit cut-offs, assignment of healthcare system and economic classifications from external sources (Böhm et al., World Bank), a decision rule for reconciling OA1 with domain scores, and tabular presentation of extracted variables and therapeutic interventions (text_5). However, the manuscript never describes methods for handling missing data or missing summary statistics (e.g., for guidelines lacking specific extracted variables), so the data preparation methods are only partially reported.

elements.quote: We identified 3,676 records from databases and 231 from grey literature. We screened 2,486 references and excluded, 2,093 that were not relevant
elements.reason: Numbers identified (3,676 + 231), after duplicate removal/screened (2,486), and excluded at title/abstract screening (2,093) are reported, and the PRISMA flow diagram (figure_3, text_13) shows the same figures.

elements.quote: We reviewed 393 documents in full text and excluded 322 of them with reasons.
elements.reason: Full-text assessments (393) and exclusions with reasons (322) are reported; the flow diagram (figure_3) lists the exclusion reasons (reviews, clinical research, public health guidelines, etc.).

elements.quote: Seventy-one CPGs were included, 45 were published in English, 7 in Chinese, 7 in Italian, 5 in Spanish, 5 in German, and 2 in French

No ongoing studies or associated reports are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence; this review included published CPGs only, so the conditional requirement does not apply.
This is the first version of the living review, not an update of a previous review; text_7 states the update process 'will be launched after the publication of this first review version.'
Screening was performed manually by reviewers (text_5); no automation tools were used, so distinguishing human vs automated exclusions does not apply.

elements.quote: We reviewed 393 documents in full text and excluded 322 of them with reasons. Seventy-one CPGs were included... Figure 1 displays the selection process through the PRISMA statement flow diagram [21].
elements.reason: The manuscript reports that 322 full-text documents were excluded 'with reasons' and refers to the PRISMA flow diagram (Figure 1), but the retrieved evidence does not cite individual excluded studies or list the specific reason for each exclusion; details appear to be deferred to the figure/supplementary material, which are not available as evidence.

elements.quote: Seventy-one CPGs were included, 45 were published in English, 7 in Chinese, 7 in Italian, 5 in Spanish, 5 in German, and 2 in French [24-95]
elements.reason: All 71 included guidelines are cited via the reference range [24-95], covering the full set of included studies.

elements.quote: Table 1A and Table 1B highlight the characteristics of the included CPGs.
elements.reason: Characteristics of all included CPGs are presented in Tables 1A and 1B, with detail on scope, country, developer, methodology, and implementation tools (text_5, text_9, text_13).

elements.quote: Therapeutic Interventions | Included Rapid Guidelines (RGs): Total number 71 (100%) ... Ventilatory Support: Invasive Mechanical Ventilation | 38 (54%)
elements.reason: An additional table (Table 2) summarises therapeutic interventions for each of the 71 included guidelines, organised by intervention and quality category.

elements.quote: Table 1B. Characteristics of eligible rapid guidelines for critically ill people with COVID-19 23-94
elements.reason: AGREE II quality assessments per guideline are reported (mean domain scores and which CPGs scored ≥60% per domain, plus overall recommendations in text), and Table 1B is referenced for AGREE II results; however, full per-study domain-level and overall judgements are not visible in the retrieved evidence, only summaries.

elements.quote: The scoring or rating of each CPG was performed using a 7-point Likert scale and a comments section. Discrepancies in the scoring were resolved by focus group discussions facilitated by a CPG methodologist (YSA).
elements.reason: The methods describe how AGREE II appraisals were conducted, but no justifications for individual risk-of-bias/quality judgements per study are presented in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Two reviewers conducted independent quality assessment of each eligible CPG with the AGREE II instrument
elements.reason: The included 'studies' are clinical practice guidelines appraised with AGREE II, not primary studies with outcome-specific results; outcome-specific risk-of-bias judgements do not apply.

elements.quote: The AGREE II standardized domain scores for the first overall assessment (OA1) had a mean of 43% (SD 20.82%). Fourteen CPGs (20%) scored greater than 60%.
elements.reason: This review of clinical practice guidelines reports group-level summary statistics (means, SDs, counts, proportions) for each assessed outcome/domain across guidelines, plus detailed tabulated per-guideline data (Tables 1A, 2, 3).

No effect estimates with measures of precision (e.g., confidence intervals) are reported for any outcome; only descriptive statistics (means, SDs, frequencies) are provided. Although the unit of analysis is guidelines rather than intervention studies, no comparative effect estimates or precisions appear in the evidence.

elements.quote: The AGREE II standardized domain ratings are summarized in Table 3.
elements.reason: Results presented in text are also provided in structured tables (Table 1A/1B for characteristics, Table 2 for therapeutic interventions, Table 3 for AGREE II domain scores), fulfilling the tabular display requirement.

elements.quote: The variables were extracted to an online Google sheet then later presented in tabular formats
